subject: Discrepancy on Feb invoice — unexpected token overage (Stellar Corp)
messages:
From: Javier Rodriguez <javier@stellarcorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Invoice Feb 2026 — unexpected token overage

Hi Marissa,

We received the Feb invoice (attached) and are seeing a ~38% higher charge on usage tokens than we expected based on our internal meter. I attached the usage_export we pulled from our system (usage_report_stellarcorp_q1.csv) and the invoice (invoice_202602.pdf).

Quick details: our app tags requests with customer_id=stellar and we track tokens-per-session; our internal total for Feb is ~1,220,000 tokens but your invoice shows 1,690,432 tokens. That's ~470k tokens difference. Can you help reconcile?

We're on a monthly bill cycle and have a renewal conversation next week — we need to understand whether this is a Jasper-like billing spike or a metering mismatch.

Thanks,
Javier Rodriguez
Finance Lead, Stellar Corp

Attachment: invoice_202602.pdf (PDF, 34KB)
Attachment: usage_report_stellarcorp_q1.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Javier Rodriguez <javier@stellarcorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice Feb 2026 — unexpected token overage

Hi Javier — thanks for sending these over and sorry for the surprise. I've looped in our billing and usage engineering folks so we can reconcile quickly.

Next steps:
- Rishi will pull request-level logs for Feb and compare token counts to the invoice meter.
- Lauren will review the invoice line items and check for any one-time charges/rounding effects.
- We'll aim to respond with an initial reconciliation by EOD Fri (27 Feb). If we find an actionable cause on our side we'll propose a credit and mitigation plan.

Can you confirm whether you have any background jobs that might have retried requests during Feb (e.g., automated retry/cron runs), or any internal key rotations that generated new API keys? That helps narrow down duplicate attribution.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 08:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice Feb 2026 — initial usage log pull

Quick summary of what I pulled this morning:
- Pulled per-request meter logs for account_id=stellarcorp across 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-28.
- Total tokens billed on our side: 1,691,024 (matches invoice within rounding).
- Notable: between 2026-02-11 02:07:00 UTC and 2026-02-11 02:18:00 UTC there are ~47k repeated requests from the same API key (key suffix: ..3f9a). Request pattern: same prompt repeated with 5–6 retries within a minute.
- Also saw several requests from an untagged key created 2026-02-03 (key suffix ..b12c) that is not present in the Stellar CSV. That key accounts for ~120k tokens.

Hypotheses:
1) Retries/duplicate jobs explain ~47k tokens.
2) Untagged/rotated key explains ~120k tokens (different key not included in customer export).
3) Rounding/aggregation differences and truncation of streaming tokens could explain the rest (~200–300k) — we need to reconcile per-request tokens with customer sessions.

I'll export a redacted log with timestamps and token counts for your team to cross-check. If Stellar confirms the untagged key is theirs (e.g., an internal service or dev key), we can reclassify usage and consider a one-time adjustment. If it's not theirs, we'll keep investigating.

Attaching: redacted_usage_lines_feb11.txt (text, 6KB)

- Rishi

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Javier Rodriguez <javier@stellarcorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 16:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice Feb 2026 — reconciliation and credit proposal

Hi Javier — thanks for your patience. We completed an initial reconciliation. Key findings:

- Invoice tokens (1,691,024) match our meter.
- We identified three contributors to the delta vs your internal export:
  1) Duplicate retries on 2026-02-11: ~47,312 tokens (same API key, automated job retried due to transient 504s).
  2) Untagged API key created 2026-02-03: ~119,876 tokens. Often happens when a service rotates keys without copying tags.
  3) Metering/aggregation differences: streaming tokens and how your export buckets sessions vs our per-request meter — estimated ~201,812 tokens.

Proposed remediation:
- One-time billing credit of $2,300 (applied to the Mar invoice) to cover the duplicate retries and an operational goodwill gesture for the metering friction.
- We can reclassify usage for the untagged key if Stellar confirms ownership and wants it scoped to the same project. That would not change the invoice total but will affect attribution for quota/usage reports.
- Action items to avoid recurrence: enforce key tagging during rotation, enable server-side retry-idempotency, and configure the billing/usage alert we can provision for you (threshold + daily email).

Please confirm if you accept the credit. If so we will issue a credit memo and reflect it on your next statement; if you'd prefer an immediate refund/adjustment we can escalate to finance but it may add 3–5 business days to process.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Manager, Billing Operations
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Attachment: credit_calculation_202602.xlsx (XLSX, 8KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Javier Rodriguez <javier@stellarcorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 15:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice Feb 2026 — next steps and confirmation

Hi Javier — following up on Lauren's note.

Summary + ask: we confirmed the invoice reflects real meter counts. We will apply a one-time $2,300 credit against the February invoice to cover the duplicate retries and the operational friction around metering differences.

To proceed:
- Please reply to confirm you accept the credit and whether you want us to reclassify the untagged key to your project (we will need the key id: suffix ..b12c confirmed as yours).
- Optional: we can set up a 30-minute postmortem call to walk through logs and recommend alerts/SDK best practices — I can schedule with our Platform Reliability team.

Thanks again for raising this — we'll make the adjustment promptly on receipt of confirmation.

Best,
